faq: What formula is used?
Gallons = miles ÷ mpg. Nothing hides in it: your two inputs and one division.
UK gallons?

This calculator uses US gallons. A UK gallon is about 20% larger (4.54609 L vs 3.78541 L), so the same journey needs fewer UK gallons — 20.0 US gal ≈ 16.7 UK gal. Mixing them is the classic transatlantic fuel error.
Does the route include live traffic?
No. Traffic is inside your real-world mpg if you enter it honestly.
Why is road distance longer than straight-line?
Roads wind, and fuel is burned on road miles. Enter the road distance.
Can route results change over time?
Your mpg changes with load, season and maintenance. Measure it per fill-up and this stays accurate.
Is this the same as Liters Needed?
Same division, different unit system: that tool runs on km and L/100 km. 20.0 US gal = 75.7 L if you need the translation.
How much reserve should I plan?
The calculator gives the journey's need. Prudent planners arrive with a reserve — the Fuel Stop Planner exists to place the stops that guarantee it.
My trip computer shows a different mpg.
Trust the fill-up method: gallons bought ÷ miles since the last fill. Trip computers flatter by a few percent on many cars.
What about diesel or LPG?
The division is fuel-agnostic — miles ÷ the vehicle's stated economy in its unit. Diesel cars often post mpg figures petrol drivers envy; the arithmetic is the same.
Reserve in the tank versus reserve in the plan?
Both: the plan's margin plus arriving with fuel aboard. The calculator sizes the journey; prudence is added by you, deliberately.
